**Long-audio processing needs a chain of grounded intermediate artifacts.** Start with audio quality and speech detection, then ASR with timestamps and speaker diarization. Segment topics using text and discourse changes while keeping sentence and speaker boundaries intact. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04356) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084)

Summaries should link to their supporting time spans. Candidate clips need enough local context to preserve the speaker's meaning: cutting off “I do not recommend” before the recommendation changes the claim. A fixed 60-second target should not force a cut through a qualification.

**“Viral” is uncertain; coherence and usefulness are testable.** Rank candidates by audience relevance and complete ideas, then evaluate human preferences rather than promising virality. Verify names, quantities, and quotations against audio, especially when ASR confidence is low.

Chunk a three-hour recording with overlap and reconcile duplicated boundaries. Evaluate each stage separately: transcription errors, speaker attribution, chapter boundaries, summary faithfulness, and clip quality. A polished summary can conceal a transcription mistake, so retain the source path instead of treating each generated intermediate as unquestionable truth.

**Technical details and references.**

Run audio-quality checks/VAD, ASR with timestamps, and diarization. Segment topics using lexical/embedding changes plus discourse cues, preserving sentence/speaker boundaries. Build chapter summaries from timestamped evidence and generate candidate 60-second clips with complete local context. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04356) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084)

Rank clips for coherence, information value, and audience relevance; “viral” is an uncertain prediction, not a guaranteed property. Avoid cutting away negation or qualifications. Verify names, numbers, quotes, and timestamps against audio, and let users inspect source spans. Evaluate diarization error, ASR entity accuracy, chapter boundary quality, summary faithfulness, and human clip preferences. Process chunks with overlap and reconcile boundary duplicates instead of summarizing three hours in one unsupported compression step.
